title: Mark Zuckerberg says TikTok slowed Meta's growth
summary: At the FTC antitrust trial, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg testified that TikTok was a major competitive threat that caused Meta's growth to "slow down dramatically" after it rose to popularity. He said TikTok has remained a top focus for Meta and discussed shifts in social media growth dynamics and Meta's efforts to return to "OG Facebook" network-driven features.
content:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg testified in the U.S. Federal Trade Commission antitrust trial that TikTok’s rapid rise represented a significant competitive risk to Meta. According to Bloomberg and other outlets, Zuckerberg said the short-form video app was a "top priority" and a "highly urgent" threat when it arrived in 2018.

The reports come from a packed first week of testimony in the FTC’s case, which seeks to show Meta’s acquisitions and conduct harmed competition. If the agency prevails, remedies could include structural changes such as spinning off Instagram or WhatsApp from Meta.

Zuckerberg admitted on the stand that TikTok’s arrival had a direct impact on Meta, saying the company observed that its "growth slowed down dramatically" when TikTok became popular. He added that the ByteDance-owned app has continued to be an important focus of Meta’s competitive efforts in the years since.

ByteDance purchased Musical.ly in 2017 and merged it into TikTok the following year. Around the same time Meta (then Facebook) stopped reporting standalone Facebook user counts in its quarterly filings and shifted to a "family of apps" metric that combined Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp — a change critics say obscured slowing growth at the flagship app.

Zuckerberg also addressed how social platforms grow, commenting on the evolving role of network effects. He argued that it has become less important for social apps to rely solely on connections between friends and family to achieve scale, noting that "the apps now serve primarily as discovery engines. People can take that content to messaging engines." The comment underscores a shift toward content discovery and short-form video as primary engagement drivers.

At the same time, Facebook is attempting to lean back on traditional network effects. The company has been rolling out features designed to make it easier to connect with friends, including a revamped Friends tab to highlight friend requests and activity. In January Zuckerberg told investors that a "return to OG Facebook" — emphasizing personal connections and networks — is a key objective for 2025.

The testimony is part of a broader examination of Meta’s competitive behavior and strategic decisions amid changing consumer habits and rival platforms’ growth. The coverage of the trial has highlighted how disruptive new entrants like TikTok can force legacy platforms to alter product strategy, reporting metrics and competitive priorities.

In Meta’s antitrust trial on Wednesday, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg testified that TikTok’s success was a risk to Meta’s business, saying the short-form video app was a “top priority” and a “highly urgent” competitive threat when it arrived in 2018, according toBloombergandotheroutlets.

The reports come from a packed first week of testimony in the U.S. Federal Trade Commission’s trial against the social networking giant. If the FTC’s lawyers prevail, the trial could potentially require Meta to spin out Instagram or WhatsApp as separate companies.

Notably, Zuckerberg admitted on Wednesday that TikTok’s arrival had directly impacted Meta, saying his company had observed that its “growth slowed down dramatically” when TikTok became popular. He also said the ByteDance-owned app has continued to be a focus of Meta’s competitive efforts for several years.

ByteDancepurchasedMusical.ly in 2017, andmergedit with TikTok the following year. Around the same time, Meta (then known as Facebook)stopped reporting Facebook’s user numbersin its quarterly reports, shifting to a new “family of apps” metric that encompassed Instagram and WhatsApp. The change was designed to hide the fact that Meta’s flagship app was seeing slowing growth.

Zuckerberg made another interesting comment during the trial in response to a question about social media platforms’ “network effects.” He said it’s become less important for social media apps to leverage connections between friends and family to grow.

“The apps now serve primarily as discovery engines,” Zuckerberg told the court. “People can take that content to messaging engines.”

At the same time, however, Facebook is trying to return to its “OG roots”by turning once again to those network effects. The company recently released new features designed to make it easier to connect with friends, includinga revamped Friends tabthat highlights friend requests and activity. In January, Zuckerberg told investors that a “return to OG Facebook” was a key goal for 2025.
